title: max-autotune compile (no cudagraphs)
description: One argument: torch.compile(model, dynamic=False) -> torch.compile(model, dynamic=False, mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs"); identical math, nothing else changed.
reflection: val_bpb 0.980496 vs the 0.981817 baseline, -0.0013 (~1.6 sigma on the 8e-4 arm-to-arm floor). Throughput is the real, non-noisy measurement: 1192 steps / 312.5M tokens vs 1168 / 306.2M, i.e. +2.1% tokens at 1.033M tok/s (was 1.020M), MFU 41.86% vs 41.00%. Mean-last-60 train loss 2.7556 vs 2.758 - both metrics agree on the sign. Peak VRAM 72.6GB vs 66.2GB (autotuning picks templates with bigger workspaces), and total wall clock 504s vs ~330s: autotuning 32 GEMM shapes costs ~3 minutes of startup, which is NOT charged against TIME_BUDGET since total_training_time only accumulates for step > 10. The honest read: the +2.1% token gain is real and deterministic, but by this cell's calibration (~0.03-0.04 bpb per doubling of tokens) it predicts about -0.0013, which is exactly what I got - so the whole delta is the extra tokens and there is no separate numerical effect. This closes throughput-at-fixed-math: the remaining kernel headroom on this box is small, cuBLAS was already near-optimal, and the only autotunable hot shapes are the MLP/lm_head GEMMs (FA3 is a separate kernel and untouched). Nobody should spend another slot on compile modes; cudagraphs is the only untried variant and it fights the fresh dataloader tensors and per-step LR mutation.
